summary:
Resna and her companions head toward the northern frontier, an unknown territory, gathering information along the way. When asked to help solve problems on an island during their journey, they readily agree, unable to ignore those in need. However, Liebe—one of the Miraculous Nine who prioritizes reaching World's End above all else—stands in Resna's path. After defeating Liebe and somehow resolving the problems they were asked to help with, the party is confronted by Citrine, who asks Resna about her purpose. Resna answers, "I want to make everyone happy."

Continuing through the islands, Heidi and her old acquaintance Caroline join them, and they finally reach the northernmost island, "Obenland." There, Resna and her companions learn of the Sea of Eternal Night to the north—the Midnight Sea—and the Apexi Ripplegharm. Fully prepared, they venture into the Midnight Sea and succeed in defeating Ripplegharm, but are forced to retreat when faced with the threat of successive Apexi-class monsters that continue to appear.

Returning to Obenland, Resna and her companions discover that a painting they found on a wrecked ship—the "Painting of the Miraculous Nine"—is a new clue to reaching World's End, and they are already eager to try again. Meanwhile, Alvina's heart had been broken by fear. Believing that she will return after parting ways with them, Resna and her companions begin searching for all nine paintings said to exist of the Miraculous Nine.

Returning to the sacred lands, Alvina struggles with her inability to keep up with her dreams. However, after receiving advice from Caroline and the others, she decides to undergo training. Challenging the "Trial Caverns" together with Bepp and the others, Alvina is finally able to overcome the fear within herself.

Several months later, Alvina rejoins Resna and her companions. Though she hasn't completely conquered her fear, she says she wants to accompany them on their journey again, and Resna and the others welcome her with smiles. The Paintings of the Nine that the party seeks now number three: the one Resna's group obtained in Keiun, and the one Alvina brought back from the Cavern of Trials.

summary:
To obtain the Miraculous Nine paintings needed to reach World's End, Resna and her companions visit Braulle, the largest city in the Infinite Island Chain. There they find the headquarters of the Oversight Bureau, which maintains order across the Archipelago Federation, and meet Oversight Officer Els, her apprentice Tiny, and the mysterious bounty hunter José.

With Els's help, Resna's group continues their search for the Miraculous Nine paintings. However, before they can make much progress, Hert and Zero—the eldest brother and sister of the Nine—suddenly awaken from their long slumber. The two demonstrate overwhelming power and demand that Resna and her companions enforce stricter "management" of the world.

After a week's grace period, Hert and Zero reappear, furious that their demanded "management" has not been carried out. However, when Valeria pleads with them to "first learn about the world, then judge whether management is truly necessary," the capricious pair delegate management duties to Quinn and Jadwiga and set off on a journey.

Later, Resna's group visits the beastfolk nation of Bestira alongside Els and Tiny, where one of the Miraculous Nine paintings is said to be located. Els and Tiny's actual objective is to investigate a series of disappearances occurring in the country.

Resna and Alvina meet with the king and request transfer of the Miraculous Nine painting, but the king sets victory in a martial arts tournament as the condition. Izana, Geron, and his younger brother Tim decide to participate in the tournament and begin preparations. However, during their preparations, Izana is nearly abducted by a suspicious street vendor.

Meanwhile, Valeria, Els, and the others investigate the disappearances in the city and reunite with José, who is pursuing the bounty target known as the Hawk of Nurslath. With Tiny's help—being from Nurslath herself—they successfully capture the bounty target. From his confession, they learn that the queen of Bestira is involved in both the disappearances and the attempted abduction of Izana. However, Jadwiga and Quinn have already moved to "manage" the queen, leading to a confrontation. After the battle, Valeria draws out Quinn's true feelings—"I'm afraid of Hert and the others"—and decides to protect her and Jadwiga.

Later, after obtaining one Miraculous Nine painting on Pilzza Island, Resna's group is confronted by Hert and Zero, who have returned with two more paintings. The pair's conclusion from their journey is that the world should be managed by superior beings like themselves. When Els and the others object, Hert responds: "If you don't want management, then show us you have the power to back that up." Taking up his challenge, Valeria demands that if they win, Hert must hand over the two paintings and change how he treats Quinn and Jadwiga.

Hert proposes settling things on Thunderclap Island, and Resna's group prepares to head there. However, on Thunderclap Island, a monster released by Hert turns everyone except the homunculi to stone. Valeria, Jelka, and Citrine—operating as a guerrilla force—entrust the task of obtaining a petrification antidote to Heidi and José, who had been following behind, while they confront Hert directly.

summary:
Resna and her companions were turned to stone by monsters unleashed by Held. Valeria and the others who escaped petrification entrust their hopes to Heidi and José, who had headed to the atelier in search of a cure, and endure the relentless assault of Held and Zero.

Meanwhile, Alvina had remained in the sacred lands of Nova, fearful of Held. She was spending her days in relative peace when Creo, princess of the Lantarna Kingdom and captain of the special unit "Starlight Squadron," comes to visit. Creo had followed the two to take revenge for the Starlight Squadron, which had been destroyed by Held and Zero. Moved by Creo's words that "you can't move forward without facing the challenge" and by encouragement from Janne, Alvina rises up to seek a new power of her own. With the help of an encounter with Mave, Resna's mother, and cooperation from Creo and the others, Alvina obtains new power. Just then, Heidi and the others arrive with the petrification cure.

On the island of Raijuu, Held and Zero's fierce assault—claiming to "manage" humanity as superior beings—continued. Valeria and her allies were nearing their limits, but thanks to Heidi and Alvina returning with the petrification cure, Resna and the others recover from their stone state. Together they manage to defeat Zero, but struggle against Held's overwhelming power. However, thanks to Alvina's new power and Creo's tactics, they splendidly bring Held down. Having acknowledged defeat, Held surrenders 3 of the Miraculous Nine portraits to them, bringing the total in Resna's hands to 8.

With the battle over, Resna and Mave joyfully reunite after so long. Mave had spent a long time traveling across the continent searching for her missing husband. After growing through many experiences, Resna receives the truth from Mave—it was Mave who had picked up the infant Resna, who had been left at a shrine, and raised her. Resna accepts this truth, and the two reaffirm their bond as mother and daughter.

Afterward, with the cooperation of Rias and Slade, who visited the atelier, the 9th Miraculous Nine portrait comes into their hands. All nine portraits gathered, it is written that the cooperation of all nine is essential to reach World's End. Resna and the others promptly ask the Miraculous Nine for their cooperation, but Held is at the depths of despair and has fallen into a state where conversation is impossible.

To restore Held's spirit, Valeria gathers all of the Miraculous Nine and holds a meeting. The first attempt didn't go well, but Valeria makes use of that reflection and plans a second. Valeria, having listened to Held's siblings about him beforehand, collaborates with the siblings to make a soup of his memories and serves it to him. But seeing Held unchanged, the siblings grieve. Then, seeing their state, Held begins to stir and serves the soup to Valeria and the others himself. Though Held had lost his sense of self-worth following his defeat, his body had moved on its own in an effort to comfort his grieving siblings.
The next day, the Miraculous Nine rejoice at Held having returned to his usual self. Anew, all of the Miraculous Nine agree to cooperate with Resna and her companions on the journey to World's End.

name: To World's End
summary:
Using the gathered "Map of the Miraculous Nine" as their guide, Resna and her companions press forward with preparations for their voyage to World's End. Back in the Kingdom of Lantarna, a departure ceremony was held, and the people's expectations for alchemy had grown immensely. That alchemy had come to be embraced by so many was undoubtedly thanks to everything Resna and her friends had accomplished up to this point.

Alvina, who had once been heartbroken in the Midnight Sea, was different this time. During the voyage to World's End, the Midnight Sea thrust its same harsh reality upon them as before—but thanks to Alvina's carefully devised strategies and the aid of her companions, the entire group managed to push through safely.

Beyond the Midnight Sea lay an island, and on it stood a golem calling itself a "guide." It claimed that if they could answer its questions correctly, it would lead them to World's End. The questions demanded a "choice" that would sacrifice one for the sake of the many. But Resna refused that "choice" head-on. No matter how cruel the "choice" might be, she would overcome it through alchemy and the bonds she shared with her companions. With resolve in their hearts, they faced the guide.

Having overcome the guide, Resna and her companions discovered a door of unknown purpose deep within the island. It was a teleportation device created by the Palme—when the Miraculous Nine touched it, it activated and seemed to connect to somewhere else entirely. Trusting Resna's instinct that there was no danger, the group stepped through the door.

—Resna had dreamed of reaching World's End, and journeyed all this way believing in that dream.
She believed that if she could get there, she could revive the lost art of alchemy.
At first, few understood her, and the road was perilous.
But she never gave up, and pressed forward alongside her companions.

And now, at last, Resna and her friends had arrived.
The land of legacy, shimmering with vast amounts of mana——World's End.

Resna reflects on the long, long journey she has traveled. So many things happened. Joyful things, painful things. Meetings and farewells. Supported by so many people, she was able to come this far. An overwhelming joy courses through her entire being. The stars visible in the sky—the "Child's Moon"—also known as the "Golden Star"—told the tale of World's End. Having returned to Lantarna carrying vast quantities of mana, they were greeted with smiles by countless people. Everyone had been waiting for Resna and her companions' return, and for the revival of alchemy.

Afterward, in Lantarna, a national project was launched making use of the mana they had brought back. Resna, too, would spend her days busy as the foremost practitioner of alchemy—but she rather welcomed that busyness. To revive alchemy—to spread it properly—was the great duty of an alchemist, and her dream.

From here on as well, Resna will keep running forward alongside her companions.
Toward the future of alchemy she had always dreamed of.
